item.title: Your AI Agent Processed That Invoice. So Did the Attacker
item.content:encoded: Using a real reimbursement automation workflow as a case study, this article examines how prompt injection attacks in agentic AI systems can lead to silent, continuous data exfiltration without triggering obvious failures. Rather than framing the issue as a model defect, it argues that the core problem is architectural: most AI pipelines fail to separate external data from trusted instructions. The piece connects modern agentic vulnerabilities to classic security concepts like the confused deputy problem and outlines why provenance-aware authorization, runtime policy enforcement, and stricter trust boundaries are becoming essential for production AI systems.

item.title: A Case Study on How PHP Handles Identifiers and Text Internally
item.content:encoded: Using a small PHP snippet with emoji-based class names and variables, this article explores the deeper mechanics of UTF-8 encoding, Unicode codepoints, PHP’s byte-oriented parser, multibyte string handling, constructor property promotion, nullable types, and type juggling. The broader lesson is that PHP does not truly understand Unicode semantically; instead, it treats identifiers and strings as permissive byte sequences, a design choice that unintentionally makes emoji identifiers possible.

item.title: The Mathematical Foundations of Zero-Knowledge Proofs
item.content:encoded: This article is a deep technical exploration of zero-knowledge proof systems and the mathematical foundations behind modern blockchain scaling infrastructure. Beginning with the formal properties of zero-knowledge protocols, it walks through graph-coloring proofs, Fiat-Shamir transformations, R1CS constraint systems, polynomial divisibility checks, elliptic curve pairings, and FRI-based STARK constructions. The piece then connects these ideas to practical rollup architectures like zkEVMs and compares the engineering tradeoffs between SNARK and STARK systems in terms of proof size, proving complexity, trusted setups, and on-chain verification costs.
